metadata.summary: Background: The molecular mechanisms underlying heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) (HF-MI) remain incompletely understood, and whole-transcriptome profiling studies hold significant promise for disease prevention and treatment. Methods: Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on post-MI patients with and without HF to analyze differentially expressed mRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, along with functional enrichment analysis. Co-expression networks linking lncRNA-mRNA and circRNA-mRNA pairs, as well as ceRNA networks involving lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA and circRNA-miRNA-mRNA interactions, were constructed for differentially expressed (DE) RNAs. Key lncRNAs were validated by RT-qPCR. Transcriptional factor-lncRNA networks were constructed, and key relationships were verified using RIP-PCR. Results: Patients with HF-MI exhibited marked elevation of NT-proBNP and significant reduction in LVEF%. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed 228 DE-mRNAs, 700 DE-lncRNAs, and 1188 DE-circRNAs in HF-MI compared to non-heart failure patients (NHF-MI). Construction of the ceRNA network identified hsa-miR-6089 and hsa-miR-6771-5p as key miRNAs in the lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network, while hsa-miR-1207-5p and hsa-miR-10392-3p were key miRNAs in the circRNA-miRNA-mRNA network. PVT1, SNHG5, TTN-AS1, HCP5, and OIP5-AS1 were identified as the five key DE-lncRNAs, with PVT1/SNHG5 showing upregulation and TTN-AS1/HCP5/OIP5-AS1 exhibiting downregulation. The transcription factor-lncRNA network primarily involves GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1, with validated associative interactions. Conclusion: This study systematically mapped the regulatory network of HF-MI, revealing the roles of the GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1 regulatory axes in HF-MI, thereby providing a basis for exploring novel therapeutic strategies.

metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

metadata.summary: Background: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) followed by a reperfusion results in a phasic response by cardiac macrophages. During the first 7 days after AMI, macrophage populations exhibit dynamic phenotypic changes. Ultimately, inflammatory damage results in ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. Macrophages are critical to cardiac function and long-term prognoses. Objective: Elucidate the spatiotemporal behavior of specific macrophage subtypes during  AMI and identify novel genes with prospective therapeutic potential. Methods: We implement an IRI mouse model of AMI to assess cardiac macrophage behavior during AMI. RCM were isolated using flow cytometry and analyzed with NanoString. Pathway enrichment analysis annotated statistically significant genes. We employed transcriptome-wide, spatiotemporal analysis of cardiac tissue samples during  AMI.

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed using the Parse Biosciences Evercode platform.

metadata.summary: The mammalian heart derives from different fields of progenitors, but the mechanisms driving their distinct establishment remain unclear. This study provides a non-cell-autonomous heterochronic model for the establishment of cardiac progenitor fields, implicating a Hedgehog-dependent differentiation delay. This paradigm may support the coordinated development of complex organs broadly.

That difference sounds obvious until an experiment presents a harmonious video: many agents turn together, a scaffold gradually becomes populated, and the final frame resembles the planned pattern. The resulting images can be visually compelling even when the agents were never making independent decisions. A single external magnetic field might explain the apparent consensus. The assembly might succeed only when the task queue is uncomplicated. One robot might have been lost between camera frames, or a defective component quietly discarded. The challenge of Family 13 is to design a scientific framework in which these counterexamples do not disappear behind a good-looking animation.  The proposed research joins self-organized arrangement, distributed manufacturing assignment, asynchronous communication, resilience under robot failure, and full-cost effectiveness. These subjects are coupled, yet they are not interchangeable. An alignment metric is dimensionless; accepted manufacturing tasks per robot-hour carry an inverse-time unit; coordination delay is measured in seconds; resilience is defined against a baseline and reported as a percentage; and cost must be computed per independently function-qualified output rather than per movement. A system can achieve a high order parameter while performing fewer tasks; it can tolerate packet loss yet consume more energy; it can retain throughput after a failure but leave an unrecovered micro-object in a sensitive region. A legitimate integration requires separate acceptance conditions for every pathway.  The mother blueprint fixes the five official topics F061–F065 and provides a circular heading-order relation as a common candidate point of departure. We preserve that relation as source lineage but do not pretend it is a universal equation for task economics or failure recovery. The additional candidate formulas in the full research monograph are proposed engineering constructions: an accepted-task denominator, task conservation equations, latency and command age, recovered throughput, and audited full cost. Their mathematical form makes assumptions testable, not true by decree. The accompanying forty-two three-dimensional curves use declared synthetic inputs and can be reconstructed from CSV files and Python code. Such reproducibility checks numerical honesty only; it never amounts to an in-vitro demonstration or a functional organ result.  This distinction is inherited from the supplied STARLI F18 organ-chip research mother: geometric accuracy is not physiological function. A well-built microassembly can fail a material, contamination, electrical or metabolic assay; an impeccably coordinated robot swarm can still be the worse instrument for building it. For Family 13, the minimum proving ground is a recoverable, nonliving five-agent microswarm with independently timed video, traceable field strength, a fully enumerated task ledger and a physical human-operated stop. Only after nonliving mechanisms survive matched controls should a separately authorized experiment even be considered. No calculation here licenses implantation, in-vivo action, clinical treatment or autonomous interaction with a human.  F061  |  SELF-ORGANIZED ARRANGEMENT OF MICROROBOT SWARMS AT THE LIMIT  Order begins as a question of attribution. Let each tracked robot have a heading angle and compute the magnitude of the mean complex unit vector. The result approaches one when headings agree, but that mathematical agreement has more than one possible cause. It may be the desired effect of local neighbor interactions. It may instead be external-field entrainment, an unrecorded leader or a video-analysis convention that systematically excludes difficult trajectories. A sophisticated swarm cannot be certified by one circular average. Alongside its order parameter it must report robot count, three-dimensional separation, contact events, excluded frames and field-drive exposure.  The most decisive experiment is not to push coupling gain upward until the curves look smooth. It is to disconnect peer information while preserving the magnetic field, illumination, container geometry and full run duration. If the group remains equally ordered, a local-coordination hypothesis has lost its most specific evidence. A second contrast reverses the externally applied field phase without disclosing the change to the controller. This challenges whether the method can distinguish learned peer adaptation from synchronization imposed by the apparatus. Both tests deserve blinded independent pose reconstruction. HOW THE FIVE FLAGSHIPS COUPLE WITHOUT ERASING THEIR SCIENTIFIC IDENTITIES  An integrated swarm manufacturing platform can be understood as an evidence graph rather than a single score. Self-organization determines whether a group finds a stable configuration. Allocation determines which agent has authority to work on which piece. Communication permits reservations and release decisions to move through the group. Resilience determines what happens when a component of the group disappears or gives invalid information. Economics determines whether the independently accepted output justifies the resources. Each relation has a different mathematical unit and an independent failure condition. A good result on one axis cannot compensate for a failure of another safety or qualification gate.  For example, strong ordering may make it easier to position many robots around a scaffold, but it can also increase crowding and collision. A more responsive local auction may raise job throughput until the communication channel saturates. Shorter messages can lower median delay while leaving rare stale commands hazardous. Spare robots can retain production under failure while increasing total energy and capital cost. The scientific project is to map those trade-offs, not to assert that coupling is beneficial by definition. A valid platform should publish the regions in which combined architecture is better, equivalent or worse than simpler alternatives.  The forty-two synthetic response surfaces in the companion PDF are organized around five deliberately separate mathematical domains. One describes how local alignment gain and communication dropout affect a dimensionless order proxy. Another studies accepted task throughput as a function of agent count and queued work. A third relates message delay and packet loss to seconds of coordination penalty. The fourth examines faulted-agent percentage and reserve capacity against retained qualified throughput. The fifth varies coordination overhead and accepted yield to produce audited cost per qualified unit. Each surface uses declared ranges, a frozen equation, and CSV values that can be regenerated from attached Python. None of these curves is fitted to cells, real robots or organ function data.  An especially important counterfactual concerns the shared field. Micro-objects can respond collectively to the same field even when no agent communicates with another. Therefore visual correlation and directional agreement are at best a preliminary observation. Separating common driving from peer intelligence requires controlled link disablement, external field recordings, matched passive and centrally controlled agents, independent three-dimensional trajectory recovery, and the ability to retain null outcomes. A local algorithm that offers no further gain over common-field control may still be useful as a simulation tool, but it cannot claim evidence of distributed robotic autonomy.  Another counterfactual concerns selection. A research team may count only the robots that stayed in focus, only the work items eventually completed, only the network messages that arrived, and only the products that passed. Four different denominators can then manufacture four attractive performance figures from one unproductive experiment. The full-attempt record should instead disclose all commissioned agents, initiated tasks, transmitted messages, untracked time, payload losses, incomplete structures and independent quality outcomes. The result may look less elegant, but it becomes a claim that another laboratory can actually test.  The two hundred Research Gates turn these vulnerabilities into invitations. A gate can ask whether the self-organized order survives the removal of peer information, whether task throughput holds after a concealed deadline burst, whether an event remains causally ordered under hidden clock drift, whether a disabled payload carrier can be retrieved, or whether lower apparent costs survive an external accountant who prices every rejected unit. Each Gate is a separate Origin, Extreme Extrapolation, Future Research Plan sequence. The conceptual and counterfactual diagrams are proposed structures to clarify scientific decisions; they are not evidence that the depicted systems exist or work.  Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos offer bounded next-generation engineering objects: a peer-link disconnect station, a dual-view collision sentinel, a task ownership ledger, a stale-command safety veto, a faulted-payload recovery tile, an independent output qualification camera, and a full-cost auditor, among other possibilities. Their common promise is not that all will succeed. It is that each can be assembled as a minimum nonliving experimental object, exposed to a concrete rival mechanism, compared fairly, and retired when it fails. A failed prototype can remain scientifically valuable if its data and reasons for retirement are reconstructable.  THE ROLE OF THE MOTHER DOCUMENTS AND THE LIMIT OF THE EVIDENCE  The official two-hundred-flagship STARLI atlas provides the F061–F065 topic identities, broad candidate relation and twelve-part study planning framework. The supplied F18 organ-chip research mother contributes a separate manufacturing-to-function boundary: placing cells precisely or producing geometric order is not evidence of an independent physiological endpoint. The STARLI smart manufacturing DOI provides source lineage for production and quality accounting. External microrobotics literature supplies methodological examples of field actuation and microfluidic engineering. These are reference and design roles, not independent confirmation of the candidate swarm advantages in this publication. Every proposed advantage remains prospective and untested.  A living-tissue claim would require separately reviewed and independently measured functional assays in an appropriate model, including sample identity, environmental exposure, contamination, viability, and material residues. None of those is supplied by a synthetic 3D curve or by the existence of a robotic assembly plan. No portion of this research working edition constitutes a clinical intervention protocol or regulatory certification. All robot actions described for the minimum validation setting remain nonliving and recoverable, with human authority and an independent hard stop. Future researchers may publish negative results, unaccounted losses, or cases in which simpler methods dominate.  The deepest inheritance of Family 13 is a method for asking a better question of complexity. When five robots appear more intelligent than one, what new capability has actually been demonstrated, by whom was it independently measured, what simpler apparatus could have done the same job, and which adverse event forces the research claim to stop? Background and PurposePrehospital stroke recognition remains suboptimal, with nearly one-third of strokes unidentified before hospital arrival, and neurological assessment being inherently subjective, with substantial interobserver variability even among certified clinicians. APOLLAI, a multimodal artificial intelligence system, was developed to detect stroke-related neurological deficits from video and audio recordings. We compared the diagnostic performance of APOLLAI and emergency medical services (EMS) personnel against an expert consensus reference standard.

MethodsIn this prospective study, video recordings of 295 patients with suspected stroke (mean age, 70.3{+/-}13.3 years) were obtained at Nimes University Hospital (August 2023-July 2025). Five National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale items (best gaze, facial palsy, motor arm, aphasia, dysarthria) were independently annotated by seven certified stroke neurologists, combined into consensus labels using the Dawid-Skene algorithm, and separately assessed by EMS personnel (mean of 15 raters per patient). APOLLAI, a multimodal machine-learning framework that combines computer vision, audio-based deep learning, and a final support vector machine (SVM) fusion classifier, was evaluated against EMS using sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

ResultsInterrater agreement among the seven neurologists was moderate overall (mean {kappa}=0.541; range, 0.367-0.732), indicating an intrinsic difficulty of neurological assessment. APOLLAI showed higher sensitivity than EMS for all five neurological tasks and for the global assessment (78.5% versus 59.4%), with broadly comparable specificity (87.0% versus 85.9% for the global assessment). AUC values ranged from 0.839 (facial palsy) to 0.966 (best gaze), with a global AUC of 0.882.

ConclusionsAPOLLAI demonstrated higher sensitivity than EMS personnel for detecting stroke-related neurological deficits, with preserved specificity. These findings support its potential as a standardized, scalable adjunct to prehospital stroke recognition, warranting prospective validation under real-world EMS conditions.

The family therefore requests orthogonal witnesses and blinded reference swaps. Hookean force versus indentation is valid only over a measured local elastic range; it must not be used as a universal membrane-damage law. Normalized prediction error can be compared across instruments only when the reference scale remains frozen. Complete time must include setup, readout, calibration and failed-run review. BackgroundEstimation of nephron number, an indicator of renal reserve, requires quantitative assessment of glomerular number and size in kidney biopsy specimens. We aimed to develop an automated system for quantitative measurement of glomerular areas from clinical kidney biopsy images, across diverse kidney diseases.

MethodsWe developed a two-stage deep learning system combining Faster R-CNN for glomerular detection in whole-slide images (WSIs) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. Of 114 kidney biopsies (228 WSIs), 104 were used for model development and 10 for independent final evaluation. Agreement was assessed using the F1-score for detection, the Dice coefficient for segmentation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for glomerular area measurement. Analysis was performed at 40x total magnification (2.331 m/pixel) and validated against 400x images.

ResultsIn the independent evaluation set, the artificial intelligence (AI) model achieved a mean F1-score of 0.851 for detection, compared with 0.888 among experts. For segmentation, the Dice coefficient was 0.959 {+/-} 0.011 and the per-pair ICC (2,1) for area measurement was 0.989 {+/-} 0.009; both were comparable to inter-expert agreement. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -344 m{superscript 2} (95% limits of agreement, -1904 to 1216 m{superscript 2}) between 40x and 400x measurements.

ConclusionThe two-stage model achieved glomerular segmentation and area measurement comparable to expert agreement in independent clinical data, with detection performance approaching inter-expert agreement, and provided reliable measurements at low magnification. This automated approach may facilitate large-scale quantitative kidney pathology and nephron number estimation from clinical kidney biopsies.

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrotic scar formation, disrupting electrical communication and impairing cardiac function. Conductive hydrogels have been studied to reconstruct an electroactive microenvironment for the infarcted myocardium, yet their regenerative effect is limited by the impaired function of surviving cardiomyocytes. Here, we developed a mechanoelectrically active and paintable hydrogel capable of converting cardiac motion into localized electrical stimulation to repair infarcted myocardium. The paintable nature of the hydrogel enables easy application onto irregular epicardial surfaces using a customized brush, while subsequent photocrosslinking allows selective adhesion of the hydrogel to only epicardial surfaces, not to surrounding tissues. Under cyclic loading and in contracting cardiac organoids, the hydrogel generated physiologically relevant electrical potentials, demonstrating efficient deformation-induced charge generation. In a rat MI model, the hydrogel providing electrostimulation alleviated ventricular wall thinning and fibrosis, promoted neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, and improved cardiac function. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed upregulation of genes involved in myocardial contraction and energy metabolism. As such, our study offers a minimally invasive and clinically translatable approach for cardiac repair and other tissue applications.

Hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA), a natural secondary bile acid, plays key roles in metabolic homeostasis, yet its direct cardioprotective effects in obesity-related cardiac injury remain unclear. HDCA also bound PIK3CA to inhibit PI3K-AKT-mediated inflammation. In 3D cardiac spheroids, HDCA alleviated lipotoxic injury. metadata.summary: Laminopathies comprise a diverse array of phenotypes that involve multiple organs and are caused by mutations in the LMNA gene, which encodes nuclear envelope protein lamin A (LMNA). Cardiac involvement is a prominent feature and a major cause of mortality and morbidity in laminopathies. LMNA interacts with chromatin through lamin-associated domains (LADs) and regulates gene expression. The role of the LMNA in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression in cardiac myocytes is unknown.  We conditionally deleted the Lmna gene specifically in cardiac myocytes in the mouse, isolated the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes, and characterized genomic structure and function at two levels: first, by identifying and characterizing the genome-wide CTCF binding sites by a CUT&RUN assay; and second, the chromatin conformational changes by HiC.  To determine the role of LMNA in genome organization and gene expression we integrated CTCF binding, LAD, Hi-C data with the gene expression (RNA-seq), and DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs), determined by END-Seq, in cardiac myocytes.  Compared to wild-type (WT) myocytes, LMNA deficiency increased genomic occupancy of CTCF , predominantly outside of the constitutive LADs (cLADs), and increased gene expression at the CTCF binding sites. Likewise, DSBs were highly enriched at the CTCF binding sites. However, only a small fraction of the chromatin compartments was shifted in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. LMNA-deficiency changed the organization of one-third of the topologically-associated domains (TADs). The changes were characterized by the merger of 2 or more TADs (60%), mainly in the non-LAD regions, splitting (30%), and shifting boundaries (10%). Reorganization of TADs, however, did not directly affect gene expression or the prevalence of DSBs. A remarkable effect of the LMNA deficiency was on chromatin loops, as it led to a gain of ~ 600 and a loss of ~1000 loops, whose boundaries were enriched in the CTCF binding sites. The changes affected the transcript level of ~25% of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the LMNA-deficient cardiac myocytes. The gain of the loop was associated with increased gene expression, whereas the loss of the loop had the opposite effect. A multivariate analysis showed that differential CTCF  binding  (largest), loops, and cLADs affected the transcript levels of the DEGs, whereas TADs and chromatin compartments appeared to act in concert with these factors  rather than as independent determinants.  In conclusion, LMNA regulates chromatin structure like TADs its role in  gene expression is mediated mainly through CTCF, cLADs, and loops,. The findings provide insights into the molecular pathogenesis of cardiac involvement in the diverse array of phenotypes in laminopathies.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

metadata.summary: Diabetic cardiomyopathy is a clinical condition of ventricular dysfunction, with obesity and insulin resistance as the primary risk factors. Under this condition, the heart accumulates fatty acids and encounters lipotoxicity, which impairs cardiac insulin sensitivity and leads to cardiomyopathy. Angiotensin-(1-9) is a peptide of the counter-regulatory axis of the renin-angiotensin system with cardioprotective effects in myocardial infarction. However, its role in diabetic cardiomyopathy is unknown. To explore the role of angiotensin-(1-9), we first induced lipotoxic stress in the heart by high-fat diet (HFD) feeding in mice. Angiotensin-(1-9) was then administered for four weeks using osmotic mini-pumps. Cardiac function was assessed by, and insulin sensitivity was evaluated in tissues after a bolus of insulin injection. Moreover, lipotoxic stress in vitro was modeled by high glucose medium plus palmitate in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs). We show that angiotensin-(1-9) improves myocardial function and reverts pathological cardiac remodeling in mice. Moreover, angiotensin-(1-9) enhances whole-body glucose tolerance and reduces homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). We next demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) increases insulin sensitivity in the heart and skeletal muscle but not in adipose tissue or the liver. Mechanistically, angiotensin-(1-9) does not affect insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes at baseline, while it significantly improves insulin action under lipotoxic stress through AT2 receptor (AT2R) and PKA. These findings demonstrate that angiotensin-(1-9) improves cardiac function under metabolic challenge and promotes insulin signaling in cardiomyocytes under lipotoxicity, which may shed light on the therapeutic exploration against diabetic cardiomyopathy.

observations.text: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) requires immediate postpartum recognition for primary repair. Diagnosis relies primarily on clinical examination, as endoanal ultrasound (EAUS) is rarely a bedside option. Therefore, objective diagnostic assessment is most needed during the first postpartum hours. However, it is challenging to obtain the anatomically verified data needed to develop diagnostic technologies for this clinical window. We evaluated the translation of a machine-learning-assisted impedance spectroscopy model into its intended immediate postpartum setting. The model lifecycle comprised three sequential phases: V1 development using anatomically verified data from a prospective multicenter study (N=152); V2 real-world adaptation, comprising post-market data collection, retraining (N=144) to adapt to acute physiological tissue changes, and subsequent separate evaluation (N=125); and prospective external validation of V2 in an unseen cohort (N=70). During this separate evaluation, V2 achieved 89.6% accuracy. In external validation, all examinations occurred within 4 hours of birth (94.3% within the first hour). Against subsequent EAUS, V2 achieved 86.2% sensitivity, 92.7% specificity, and 90.0% overall accuracy. The V2 model was prospectively externally validated in its intended immediate-postpartum setting, supporting ML-assisted impedance spectroscopy as an objective adjunct, and not a replacement, to clinical OASI assessment. Further validation is required to confirm generalizability.

metadata.summary: Background: Reactive oxygen species are increased across most pulmonary hypertension (PH) etiologies, resulting in increased reactive lipid dicarbonyls, which form protein adducts and impair mitochondrial function. Results: Reducing reactive lipids with 2-HOBA resulted in a ~10% reduction in RVSP, reduced diastolic dysfunction, reduced plasma lipids and ceramides, and normalized RV fatty acid oxidation that was severely impaired in the AKR-HFD and PAB models. Proteomic and RNA changes in the lungs, RV, and LV suggested reduced oxidative damage and inflammatory signaling and altered developmental and actin organization signaling; these changes are plausibly associated with the improved adaptation. Some changes were sex specific, including a 4x higher cardiac fatty acid content in males than females. Conclusions: Reactive lipid scavenging improves cardiac metabolic and diastolic function and pulmonary vascular resistance through restoration of mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative protein damage. The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

MICRONANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AT THE LIMIT  F046-F050 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0  Prospective, nonclinical research synthesis. All three-dimensional model surfaces are synthetic numerical constructions; no biological experiment, verified navigation advantage or device clearance is claimed.  Five flagship studies  F046 | Magnetically Driven Microrobot Navigation in Microchannels at the Limit. Primary endpoint: blind three-dimensional route-tracking RMSE [µm]. Minimum prototype: a sealed acrylic microchannel with inert magnetic surrogate beads, coil-current logs and an independent 3D imaging reference. Strong comparator: registered open-loop magnetic control, skilled optical stage guidance and matched passive tracer flow. Independent stop: wall contact, unbounded field gradient, temperature excursion or lost independent localization.  F047 | Microrobotic Motion in Complex Viscoelastic Fluids at the Limit. Primary endpoint: held-out trajectory error after rheological transfer [µm]. Minimum prototype: a temperature-controlled viscoelastic microchannel phantom with rheometer-calibrated relaxation spectrum and reversible magnetic drive. Strong comparator: Newtonian viscosity-matched fluid with the same geometric envelope and a fitted linear drag controller. Independent stop: unbounded elastic stress, irreversible gel rupture, unexplained sample heating or lost relaxation calibration.  F048 | Autonomous Path Planning in Multi-Obstacle Organ Chips at the Limit. Primary endpoint: collision-free completed-route proportion [%]. Minimum prototype: a transparent obstacle-rich organ-chip phantom with CAD-verified geometry and held-out obstacle layouts. Strong comparator: equal-budget A* graph search, manually registered safe routes and open-loop waypoint pursuit. Independent stop: negative clearance, forced entry into a protected chamber or unrecoverable planner uncertainty.  F049 | Swarm Collision Avoidance and Cooperative Localization at the Limit. Primary endpoint: collision-free qualified placement throughput [robots/min]. Minimum prototype: a two-to-eight agent magnetic surrogate swarm in a branching synthetic chip with independent identity-preserving tracking. Strong comparator: single-robot sequential navigation and a centralized equal-budget controller without cooperation. Independent stop: any physical collision, unassignable identity swap or loss of human override on a shared coil system.  F050 | Real-Time Correction of Microscale Navigation Error at the Limit. Primary endpoint: blind corrected position RMSE [µm]. Minimum prototype: a delay-injectable camera-and-coil bench phantom with randomized sensor dropouts and a frozen observer. Strong comparator: fixed-gain PID tracking, uncorrected dead-reckoning and a calibrated Kalman-filter comparator. Independent stop: diverging innovation residual, missed deadline, noncausal future-frame use or controller saturation.  ZENODO RESEARCH DESCRIPTION  The miniature robot that reaches the end of a microchannel has not necessarily accomplished a scientific task. Its elegant trajectory might result from a hidden pressure gradient, a change in polymer relaxation, an overly forgiving obstacle map, a switch of agent identities, or retrospective video smoothing. The harder problem is to build a navigation system whose intended motion, measured physical displacement, estimated uncertainty and independent stopping authority remain aligned when those comfortable assumptions fail. This book is an invitation to construct that evidence, not a claim that it already exists.  The research lineage begins with the supplied 200-flagship roadmap and with the earlier F18 organ-chip monograph, whose central rule is that geometric success is not physiological function. The present family carries this principle into five engineering domains: magnetic navigation in confined microchannels, viscoelastic locomotion, collision-aware route planning, group navigation under shared fields and error correction under delayed sensing. Their interfaces form a research system only if the component measurements survive independent calibration and all failed attempts remain in view.  FLAGSHIP F046 | MAGNETICALLY DRIVEN MICROROBOT NAVIGATION IN MICROCHANNELS AT THE LIMIT  Microchannel magnetic navigation begins from the physical interface confined magnetic actuation, low-Reynolds-number drag and channel-wall clearance. Its proposed primary endpoint is blind three-dimensional route-tracking RMSE [µm], evaluated in a sealed acrylic microchannel with inert magnetic surrogate beads, coil-current logs and an independent 3D imaging reference. This is not a biological efficacy metric. Every apparent improvement should be contrasted with registered open-loop magnetic control, skilled optical stage guidance and matched passive tracer flow. An honest system must stop when wall contact, unbounded field gradient, temperature excursion or lost independent localization. HOW THE FIVE FLAGSHIPS COUPLE WITHOUT MERGING THEIR CLAIMS  The first coupling crosses the boundary between magnetic force and local flow. A coil current is only a command. It cannot identify the magnetic force at the robot unless magnetic moment, orientation, field map and geometry have been measured. A visually stationary robot might be trapped by a magnet, carried by a vortex or pinned against a wall. The strongest baseline therefore includes flow-matched passive trajectories and equal-time calibrated stage guidance, with heating and recovery independently recorded.  The second coupling crosses the boundary between fluid viscosity and fluid memory. A complex medium may show shear thinning and elastic recoil simultaneously. A single fitted effective viscosity can agree with one period of actuation and fail catastrophically when the field reverses. The family therefore tests causal stress and relaxation models across varied drive periods, and treats a failure of one constitutive approximation as a reason to revise the domain, not to claim that an unmeasured new force exists.  The third coupling crosses the boundary between geometric path feasibility and executable motion. A narrow gap visible on a chip map may remain closed to a finite robot with position uncertainty, wall roughness and field-limited turning. A planner should report infeasibility when clearance is exhausted. Reporting only successful routes rewards unsafe exploration. The essential comparator is a feasible classical path search under the same map, time and actuation constraints, with a transparent definition of every initiated trial.  The fourth coupling concerns the ambiguous promise of swarm cooperation. Parallel robots can increase throughput but may share a magnetic field and influence each other through near-field forces. A formation can appear successful after the vision system swaps two identities, or after a stuck robot is removed from analysis. Independent agent identification, pairwise separation and complete population accounting are therefore part of the experiment. Cooperation needs to outperform a sequential single-robot comparator under equal resource budgets.  The fifth coupling concerns real-time correction. A Kalman filter, nonlinear observer or learned controller may create an excellent retrospectively smoothed trace by using frames that were unavailable when the coil command was issued. The true scientific unit is the causal closed loop, including acquisition, computation, communication and actuation delay. A held-out reference camera should reconstruct errors and missed deadlines without sharing information with the tested controller. When the observer diverges, a stop is more informative than an interpolated victory.  These five interfaces should be studied in a staged manner, with each subsystem allowed to fail independently. The formula pages are not a set of newly discovered laws. Every equation states a physical domain and a measurement that could invalidate it; dimensional compatibility is checked before a surface is plotted.  Forty-two three-dimensional surfaces vary two physically declared parameters and report one projected endpoint. Field gradient and pump speed determine a synthetic tracking-error surface; Deborah number and drive frequency probe fluid-memory sensitivity; obstacle fraction and map uncertainty affect simulated route success; population and field gradient probe minimum interagent clearance; and observation delay and sensor noise change corrected localization error. Model grids, axis units, numerical assumptions, csv records and a standalone Python reconstruction script are stored in the research PDF. Recalculating a numerical surface confirms its computational consistency, not its correspondence to biological measurements.  A demanding falsification program will preregister which curvature or threshold in those surfaces the experiment is supposed to test. Some curves may prove physically inaccurate. A useful result then describes the alternative physical explanation, revised domain and uncertainty rather than deleting the failed prediction. The essence of a mathematical model is its capacity to disagree with an experiment in a meaningful, reproducible way.  RESEARCH GATES AND PHOENIX PROTOTYPES  Two hundred Research Gates offer questions to successor investigators. Each follows an origin, a deliberately extreme counterfactual world and a future research plan. The origins begin in real measurement limitations; the counterworlds ask whether a system could appear to work while the hidden source of apparent success is an artifact; and the future plans establish how another laboratory could defeat both the preferred model and its strongest rival. The doors are meant to open through criticism rather than applause.  Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate instruments such as a blind field atlas, reversible magnetic navigator, chip-wall clearance sentinel, memory-aware rheology observer, autonomous recovery route, shared-field swarm monitor and causal-latency injection bench. Each is a prototype idea, not finished equipment. The minimum test requires an identifiable physical endpoint, a strong comparator, transparent control authority and a retirement condition if independent measurements disagree.  The family thereby treats restraint as part of technical progress. A route is not qualified if an agent cannot be recovered, if a collision is hidden, if a controller violates a protected region or if a supposedly online algorithm uses information from after the actuation deadline. These hard stops are not merely legal cautions; they are experimental conditions that decide whether a putative engineering advantage is meaningful.  SCIENCE, SUCCESSION AND OPEN ACCESS  The strongest legacy of this proposed program may be its negative cases. A chip branch that cannot be traversed, a polymeric fluid that defeats a Newtonian controller, a swarm that loses individual identity, and a delayed observer that fails to prevent a wall contact are each highly useful if the laboratory preserves the raw trace, reference measurement, failed assumptions and complete attempt denominator. The next researcher needs those records more than a polished best-run montage.  The research is prospective, nonclinical and bounded to inert laboratory phantoms. There is no claim of an implanted navigation system, organ-specific physiology, cell preservation, therapeutic benefit or regulatory clearance. metadata.summary: Cardiac fibrosis and metabolic dysfunction are central features of pressure overload-induced heart failure. To characterize transcriptional changes associated with disease progression and pharmacological intervention, single-nucleus RNA sequencing was performed on murine heart samples collected from sham-operated mice and mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC). Samples comprised five groups: Sham at 2 weeks after surgery, pTAC2W + vehicle, pTAC2W + PD173952, pTAC5W + vehicle, and pTAC5W + PD173952, with two biological replicates per group. In the pTAC2W cohort, PD173952 or DMSO vehicle was administered during the final 1 week before tissue collection, whereas in the pTAC5W cohort treatment was administered during the final 3 weeks. This dataset was generated to define cell type-resolved transcriptional responses to pressure overload and PD173952 treatment in the heart.

metadata.summary: Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2 (NR4A2) is a widely expressed immediate early gene induced by a host of physiological signals such as growth factors, cytokines, and neurotransmitters. In the adult mammalian heart, including in cardiomyocytes, NR4A2 mRNAs increase more than 60-fold in response to beta-adrenergic stimulation. However, the nature of the transcriptional remodeling induced by NR4A2 in the stressed heart has remained poorly investigated. We show here that NR4A2 activation in mouse cardiomyocytes leads to a rapid remodeling of the cardiac microRNA network. A total of 35 miRNAs were down-regulated, including the muscle-specific miR-133a and miR-499. On the opposite, 65 miRNAs were up-regulated, with a strong representation of miRNAs encoded within the imprinted Dlk1-Dio3 domain. Non-coding RNAs from the Dlk1-Dio3 locus are known for coordinating critical steps of cardiac development such as cardiac lineage commitment, cardiac morphogenesis, and cardiomyocyte proliferation, and for inhibiting mitochondrial function in myocytes. The findings shed light on a novel regulatory mechanism controlling cardiac homeostasis, and establish a framework to investigate further the roles played by NR4A2 in cardiac adaptation or maladaptation to various acute and pathological stress conditions.

metadata.summary: Truncating variants in desmoplakin (DSP) are a leading cause of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, a severe heart muscle disease characterized by fibrosis and life-threatening arrhythmias. Desmoplakin anchors the junctions that hold heart muscle cells together to the internal cytoskeleton, enabling the heart to withstand the force of each contraction. No targeted therapy exists, and DSP is too large for conventional gene replacement. Here we show, in explanted human hearts and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, that truncating DSP variants reduce desmoplakin RNA and protein, and that the resulting haploinsufficiency renders cardiomyocytes vulnerable to cell–cell adhesion failure under contractile stress, preceded by disruption of the cell membrane. Lowering contractile force with the myosin inhibitor mavacamten prevents this failure. Circumventing the size of DSP, CRISPR-based transcriptional activation of the endogenous gene restores desmoplakin expression and rescues adhesion. Haploinsufficiency is therefore the primary defect in DSP cardiomyopathy, and transcriptional activation offers a therapeutic strategy.

Forty-two three-dimensional numerical surfaces make assumptions visible by exposing two independent inputs against an observable such as landing error, dose error, viability loss, layer offset or function-qualified throughput. Every CSV row, model parameter and reproducing Python expression is intended to be available in the research PDF. These graphics are synthetic response surfaces, not measurements, empirical fits or guarantees of an optimum. Their scientific purpose is to make it easier for a subsequent experiment to falsify the relationship.  THE RESEARCH GATES AND PHOENIX PRINCIPLE The two hundred Research Gates invite a future generation to construct explicit counterworlds: a chip with a hidden height defect, a carrier leaving residue, a photopolymer that appears strong but suppresses survival, a robot stack made orderly by selective exclusion of failed layers, and a production pipeline whose apparent speed disappears once readout and rejection time are counted. Each gate carries a core question, an origin, an extreme extrapolation, a concrete next experiment, and a stopping condition. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos then translate some questions into minimum bench instruments: mass-balance ledgers, independent dose mirrors, fail-closed relays, calibration passports, blinded negative-world archives and reproducibility kits. None is declared constructed merely because it has been diagrammed. Their value lies in allowing future teams to build the smallest discriminating test, observe an unfavorable outcome, and publish the result without rewriting the original claim.  FROM RESEARCH WORKING EDITION TO OPEN SUCCESSOR SCIENCE The strongest inheritance is not a monument to continuous success. It is an auditable set of decisions and failures: which samples were excluded and why, which materials were used, what the separate witness measured, where the calibration failed, what the hard veto did, and whether the purported robot advantage survived a fully matched comparator. Laboratory replication is not assumed; it is a test to perform. A result may be negative, inconclusive, or restricted to a narrow phantom environment without diminishing the value of a well-posed question. The collection remains prospective and nonclinical; no description should be interpreted as demonstrated organ manufacture, animal or human intervention, medical effectiveness, regulatory authorization, or a validated autonomous bioreactor. STARLI's scientific invitation is to begin with a precise question and make it possible for a stranger to prove it wrong. metadata.summary: OCT4, SOX2, KLF4(OSK) has been demonstrated to remodel the epigenetic landscape across various cell types, facilitate cellular dedifferentiation, and play an important role in the process of aging and organ regeneration. Taken together, our data provide a differentially expressed genes between OSK and control groups in neonatal cardiomyocytes and demonstrate that the overexpression of OSK in cardiomyocytes resulted in dedifferentiation, including structural, electrophysiological, and metabolic alterations, which rendered them in a more naïve state.

metadata.summary: Muscle LIM Protein (MLP) is a key component of the cardiomyocyte Z disc that is essential for sarcomere integrity and cardiac homeostasis.  Loss of MLP function results in (cardio)myopathy phenotypes in animal models and is associated with inherited cardiomyopathies in humans. Here, we identify MLP as an evolutionarily conserved non-canonical RNA-binding protein and uncover RNA binding as a previously unrecognized mechanism involved in its cytoskeletal association. Using enhanced RNA interactome capture together with complementary biochemical approaches, we demonstrate direct RNA binding by MLP and map two short RNA-binding motifs adjacent to its LIM domains. Disrupting these motifs markedly reduces RNA association, including residues associated with cardiomyopathies. Mechanistically, RNA is required for MLP’s interactions with cytoskeletal proteins, and for the formation of higher-order MLP-containing assemblies. Consistently, RNA-binding-deficient MLP mutants exhibit impaired interactions with cytoskeletal proteins and reduced cytoskeletal retention. Our findings reveal the importance of RNA binding for the formation of MLP assemblies, and support the emerging role of RNA as a co-factor in the organization of macromolecular complexes, with potential relevance to human disease.
